content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Version Catalogs and Dependency Alignment** as part of **Packages, Modules, Dependencies, and Build Tools**. Build reproducibility depends on the Gradle Wrapper, compatible plugin/toolchain versions, declared dependency scopes, and repeatable test/build commands. Use the subtopics—Centralizing Dependency Versions, Version Catalogs, Keeping Plugin and Library Versions Compatible—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

items.title: Centralizing Dependency Versions
items.text: Centralizing Dependency Versions means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: The newest version of every plugin and library is always mutually compatible.
